title: Should we launch the new juice?

review.notes: Built on the course: model structure, colour conventions, no hard-coding, revenue drivers, DSO/DIO/DPO, CCC, indirect cash flow, contribution margin, break-even, margin of safety, discount trap, NPV. All calculations checked. Fictional company.

content.company: Sunpeak Beverages (fictional), a juice and soft drinks producer
content.briefing: The board must decide on a new juice line requiring Kz 100 million of equipment. You build the model, check working capital, find the break-even and give a clear recommendation. A sales director wants a launch discount too.

variants.text: A colleague's model has =E12*1.14 inside many formulas. What is wrong?

choices.f: Put 14% in one input cell and reference it. Changing it then updates everything.
When the rate changes, someone must find every hidden 1.14.
The number is not the issue. Hiding it is.

variants.text: How do you lay out the model?

choices.f: Inputs typed once with unit and source; outputs read clearly.

choices.t: Everything on one sheet, as needed
choices.f: Hard to check and easy to break.

choices.t: Outputs first, inputs at the end
choices.f: Order matters less than separation, but mixing them is risky.

variants.text: In your model, what does blue font mean?

choices.f: Blue inputs, black formulas, green links. Reviewers know what to change.
Formulas are black.
Links are green.

variants.text: Column G uses a different formula from the rest of the row 'to adjust one month'. What do you do?

choices.t: One formula per row; the change goes in inputs
choices.f: Consistent rows prevent hidden errors when copying.

choices.t: Leave it, with a comment explaining the change
choices.f: Comments get missed. Special columns cause errors.

choices.t: Hide column G so the row looks consistent again
choices.f: Hiding it makes the problem invisible.

variants.text: Year 1: 1,000 cases a month, list price Kz 10,000, average discount 10%. What is monthly revenue?

choices.f: Revenue = volume x net price: 1,000 x 9,000.
That uses list price. Use net price after discounts.
That is the discount, not revenue.

variants.text: Revenue Kz 500 m, cost of sales Kz 300 m, opex Kz 120 m, depreciation Kz 20 m. What is EBITDA?

choices.f: Gross profit 200 minus opex 120. Depreciation comes after EBITDA.
That deducts depreciation, giving EBIT.
That is gross profit.

variants.text: Receivables Kz 60 m, annual revenue Kz 365 m. What is DSO?

choices.f: Correct: 60 / 365 x 365.
Check the formula: receivables / revenue x 365.
That is the number of days in the year.

variants.text: DSO 60, DIO 45, DPO 30. What is the cash conversion cycle?

choices.f: CCC = DSO + DIO - DPO. Cash is tied up 75 days.
You added DPO. Payables reduce the cycle.
You subtracted DIO.

variants.text: The juice line makes a profit in year 1, but the model shows cash falling. Why might that be?

choices.t: Working capital and capex absorb it
choices.f: Indirect cash flow: profit + depreciation - working capital rise - capex.

choices.t: The model must contain an error
choices.f: Profit and cash often differ, especially in growth.
Depreciation is non-cash; it is added back.

variants.text: Next year revenue is Kz 730 m and you assume DSO stays 60 days. What receivables do you forecast?

choices.f: Receivables = DSO x revenue / 365 = 60 x 730 / 365.
That keeps last year's balance while revenue doubles.
That is the revenue.

variants.text: Price per case Kz 1,000, variable cost Kz 600, fixed costs Kz 20 m a year. What is break-even volume?

choices.f: Fixed costs / CM per unit = 20,000,000 / 400.
You divided by price, not by contribution margin.
You divided by variable cost.

variants.text: Expected volume 62,500 cases, break-even 50,000. What is the margin of safety?

choices.f: (62,500 - 50,000) / 62,500. Sales can fall 20% before losses.
You divided by break-even, not expected volume.
12,500 is units, not a percentage.

variants.text: Sales wants a 5% launch discount: price 1,000 to 950, variable cost 600. Current plan: 50,000 cases. How many cases keep total CM the same?

choices.f: Old CM 20 m / new CM 350 per case. A 5% price cut needs 14% more volume.
A 5% price cut needs much more than 5% more volume.
CM per case falls from 400 to 350, so volume must rise.

variants.text: To earn a target profit of Kz 8 m with fixed costs of Kz 20 m and CM of Kz 400 per case, what volume?

choices.f: That covers only the target profit.
That is break-even, with zero profit.

variants.text: Investment Kz 100 m. Cash flows Kz 60 m in year 1 and Kz 60 m in year 2. Discount rate 10%. NPV?

choices.f: That ignores the time value of money.
Sign reversed. Discounted inflows exceed 100.

variants.text: NPV is positive at the company's hurdle rate. What does it mean?

choices.t: The project creates value at that rate
choices.f: Returns exceed the cost of capital used.

choices.t: The project pays back in year 1
choices.f: NPV is not payback.

choices.t: Profit will be positive every year
choices.f: NPV sums discounted cash; years can still be negative.

variants.text: The sales plan shows 60% growth while the market grows 5% and the plant is at capacity.

choices.t: Flag it: test against history and capacity
choices.f: Sanity checks keep the model credible with the board.

choices.t: Accept it; sales knows the market
choices.f: Unchecked inputs make the whole model unreliable.
Better than 60%, but agree assumptions with evidence.

variants.text: Distribution costs rise with every case sold. How do you model them?

choices.t: As a variable cost per case
choices.f: Variable costs move with volume; fixed costs with inflation.
Then higher volume looks falsely cheap.
They affect contribution margin and break-even.

variants.text: The board asks: 'What if volume is 20% lower?' What should the model let you do?

choices.t: Change one input and see all outputs
choices.f: A decision tool answers 'what if' in seconds.
A good model avoids rework.
Boards need to see risk, not one number.

variants.text: Your final recommendation slide should show:

choices.f: Clear, honest and ready for a decision.

choices.t: All 40 sheets of the model, for detail
choices.f: Detail hides the message.

choices.t: Only the best-case scenario, to persuade
choices.f: Hiding risks damages trust.
